title: Resolvent Ellipsoid for Minty Set Inclusions
claim: Prior fixes and our approach both repair the zero-margin cut problem, but ours obtains the margin implicitly in one step.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, same ellipse with colored cuts and margin arrows
description: Three side-by-side panels reuse the same gray ellipse labeled E_t ⊆ X, each with a red diamond marking the Minty solution x*. Left, in black, is the 'Naive Center Cut': a dashed line through a_t with normal F(a_t) that passes right through x*, so the margin is 0. Middle, in blue, is 'Extra-gradient': a_t is moved along -ηF(a_t) to ã_t, and the cut through a_t uses the normal F(ã_t). A dashed parallel line through x* and a double-headed arrow show the margin ≥ γ_t. Right, in green, is 'Resolvent': x_t^+ and the Yosida vector g_t are returned together. The segment ηg_t is collinear with g_t, and the arrow shows margin ≥ s_t. Bold titles and italic subtitles sit above each panel. The eye goes first to the colored cut lines and the margin arrows.
caption: How extra-gradient and resolvent repair the same zero-margin obstruction. Left: the naive cut through at with normal F(at) can pass through a Minty solution x⋆, so it separates but does not protect any positive-radius neighborhood of the Minty set. Middle: extra-gradient uses the same center direction F(at) as the naive panel, but first moves from at to ˜at along −F(at) and then cuts through at with the corrected normal F(˜at); the dashed parallel support line through x⋆makes the margin explicit, and γt is the perpendicular offset between that support line and the strict cut. Right: the constrained resolvent returns x+
abstract: We study Minty set inclusion on a compact convex set $\mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ with a set-valued operator $A : \mathcal{X} \rightrightarrows \mathbb{R}^d$. Under the Minty promise, the goal is to compute $x \in \mathcal{X}$ and $u \in A(x)$ such that $\sup_{y \in \mathcal{X}} \langle u, x - y \rangle \le \varepsilon$. Our approach is geometric and we work in the fixed-scale constrained-resolvent oracle model, where a query at anchor $a$ is assumed to return a resolvent point $x^+$ together with the Yosida vector $g_Î·(a) = (a - x^+)/Î·$. We prove that each oracle response yields a sharp dichotomy: either the returned point provides an $\varepsilon$-SVI certificate, or the Yosida vector defines a strict separating normal for the Minty set. Thus, a single black-box resolvent query supplies either a certified candidate solution or a valid geometric cut. Combining this separation principle with the ellipsoid method, we obtain RESOLVENT-ELLIPSOID, an algorithm that computes an $\varepsilon$-SVI in $\mathcal{O}\!\left(\operatorname{poly}(d, \log(1/\varepsilon))\right)$ black-box oracle calls to the fixed-scale constrained resolvent. For monotone inclusions, our algorithm gives, to our knowledge, the first $\mathcal{O}\!\left(\mathrm{poly}(d, \log(1/\varepsilon))\right)$ black-box guarantee in the fixed-scale resolvent model.
